item.title: These Generals Fought for Israel. Now They See ‘Jewish Terrorism’ as the Threat.
item.description: A growing number of former Israeli generals, intelligence officials and prime ministers are accusing settlers in the West Bank of committing ethnic cleansing with government support. “Once a society behaves this way,” one said, “that society is doomed.”

item.title: Wartime Presidents of Russia and Iran Rally With Chinese and Indian Leaders
item.description: The two-day summit of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Kyrgyzstan shows the limits of U.S. economic warfare.

item.title: U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes Overnight After Monthlong Calm
item.description: The renewed attacks were the latest sign that the war that began six months ago appears far from over.

item.title: G20 Finance Officials Gather in U.S. as Iran War Grips Global Economy
item.description: The meeting is expected to focus on the ongoing economic shock from the war in Iran, which has driven up oil prices globally.

item.title: Why Larak Island Is Strategically Important for Iran
item.description: The roughly 30-square-mile island serves as a foothold for Iran’s military to advance its control over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Nonstop Russian Drones Make for Dangerous New Phase of War in Kyiv
item.description: The nearly constant air raids, a shift from years of largely overnight attacks, have left residents exhausted and on edge.

item.title: Iceland Votes to Steer Clear of European Union Talks
item.description: After divisive debate, Icelanders rejected a proposal to resume negotiations on joining the bloc in a referendum with the highest voter turnout in almost two decades.

item.title: A Principal Saved 900 Children Before His School Was Washed Away in Nepal
item.description: Rajendra Dawadi had less than 15 minutes to act on a warning of approaching floodwaters. His swift evacuation plan saved hundreds of lives.

item.title: Coral Reefs Are Running Out of Time to Recover, Research Find
item.description: Rising sea temperatures mean reefs don’t have enough time to bounce back between intense heat waves, a new report warns.
